q: The British system is based on foot (ft), pound (lb) and second (s) and is therefore also called the ____ system.
e: FPS stands for Foot-Pound-Second, the foundation of the British system.

q: The metric system consists of the CGS system and the ____ system.
e: The metric system is broadly divided into CGS and MKS frameworks.

q: The CGS system is based on centimetre (cm), gram (g) and ____ (s).
e: The second is the base unit of time in both CGS and MKS systems.

q: The MKS system is based on metre (m), kilogram (kg) and second (____).
e: The symbol 's' represents the second, the base unit of time.

q: The SI unit is just the modified form of the ____ system of units.
e: The SI system evolved directly from the Metre-Kilogram-Second system.

q: In ____, the Eleventh General Conference of Weights and Measures in France recommended an International System of Units based on the metric system of units.
e: The SI system was officially recommended and adopted in the year 1960.

q: This recommendation was accepted as SI units (full name, '____').
e: This is the French origin of the acronym 'SI'.

q: The SI unit has ____ base units and all other units are derived from these base units.
e: There are exactly seven fundamental base units in the SI system.
